result.title: Fast Construction of Inner Sphere Trees Using Machine Learning
result.summary: Collision detection for complex non-convex objects is a bottleneck in physics simulation, virtual reality, and robotics. Inner sphere trees (ISTs) answer proximity and penetration queries efficiently, but their greedy leaf-sphere construction is sequential and computationally expensive, which limits both large-scale preprocessing and runtime use. In this work, we present ML-IST, a machine-learning-based method that reformulates leaf-sphere generation as a single-shot set-prediction problem: a network predicts a fixed set of inscribed sphere candidates from multichannel voxel geometry, differentiable coverage feedback corrects the coarse prediction and fills residual gaps at finer scales, and a lightweight geometric projection enforces validity. Averaged over the test set, a single-GPU implementation of ML-IST reduces mean leaf-generation time by a factor of $2.0$--$2.6$ over single-core CPU construction across target capacities of 64--512 spheres, and qualitative results on complex models show multiscale sphere distributions that follow principal volumes and slender features. We further integrate ML-IST into the Jolt Physics and Bullet engines; in an alpha-puzzle benchmark it reaches 55.89~FPS, the highest among the compared representations (conventional IST, GImpact, and convex decomposition). These results support learned leaf generation as a practical component for fast, runtime construction of detailed collision representations.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 ML-IST，把碰撞检测所用 inner sphere tree 的叶球构造改写为「单次集合预测」：网络从多通道体素几何中一次预测固定数量的内切球候选，用可微覆盖反馈修正粗预测并补齐细尺度残差，再经轻量几何投影保证有效性；相比单核 CPU 构造，叶球生成时间约缩短 2.0–2.6 倍，并集成进 Jolt Physics 与 Bullet。
AI.relevance_reason: 其用固定数量槽位从几何输入一次性预测一组图元、并以可微覆盖反馈补足遗漏区域的思路，可能为 LVR 关注的两个问题提供可供核查的线索：latent 表示如何保留几何细节，以及如何监督表示的完整性与覆盖而非仅监督最终答案。
